info.desc: Homework is the debut studio album by the French electronic music duo Daft Punk, released on 20 January 1997 by Virgin Records and Soma Quality Recordings. The duo produced the tracks without plans to release an album. After working on projects that were intended to be separate singles over five months, they considered the material good enough for an album. .

podcast.body: Homework was not intended to be an album — Guy-Manuel and Thomas put out a bunch of individual songs without planning to collect them, but then it happened. They recorded it at home (hence the name). The album was hyped by the music press and charted in more than a dozen countries, mostly on dance charts. The only place where it was a genuine across-the-board hit was France. The single "Da Funk" sold more as a single than Homework sold as an album. "They called it that because they recorded it at Home, which makes sense."

podcast.body: This album, released approximately 20 years before the transcript's context, is considered a major turning point in 90s electronic music and music in general. It is a cult object and revolutionary because it went against the prevailing trend of complex, fast, and genre-blending electronic music of the mid-90s, returning to the slow, simple tempos characteristic of 80s techno. The album drastically reduced electronic music to its minimal expression, utilizing fewer than 30 sounds in its creation. It was initially not conceived for mass consumption, leading Virgin Records to print only 50,000 CD copies, as it was thought to be a niche album for professional rave culture, with the vinyl edition being considered more important. However, it quickly sold 650,000 CDs, exhausting the initial run immediately and prompting massive production. The album lacks a thematic or argumentative thread, being a compilation of material produced by two artists from the rave culture, eventually gathered into two vinyl discs. While its immediate influence in the late 90s and early 2000s was not substantial, as electronic music continued its complex path, its impact became evident around 2007 with the "second wave" of modern electronic music, showing significant influences on subsequent groups.

podcast.body: This was Dazpán's first album, released in 1997, and it is credited with revolutionizing modern music, especially electronic music. It became a cult hit among electronic music specialists and critics, praised for its quality and innovation, but it did not achieve significant mainstream consumption beyond a few notable instances. It marked Dazpán's first attempt at an electronic revolution. "revolucionaron la música moderna."
